daniel-claudy tour

Every feature, shot in a separate emacs -Q (only daniel-claudy + markdown-mode) with its own tmux server and two real Claude sessions in a throwaway todo-app project.

1. Session counter in the mode line2. Start a new session3. Send a prompt4. Show tool calls5. Jump to your last question6. Send only the current line7. Pick a session8. No match? That's a new session9. Queue the first prompt10. Send a selection from any buffer11. One-off question12. Usage limits13. Jump to the tmux pane14. End a session15. Resume in this pane16. Resume in a new window17. Refresh when Claude's turn ends

1Session counter in the mode line

daniel-claudy-modeline-mode

Counts every live Claude session by status. Hover lists them by name; click opens the picker.

2Start a new session

daniel-claudy-new-session

Opens a tmux window running claude in a project, names it with /rename, and gives you a buffer to type the first prompt in while it boots.

3Send a prompt

C-c C-c daniel-claudy-tmux-send-rest

Sends from the start of the current line to the end of the buffer (or the selection) to the session's tmux pane as one bracketed paste. The ⏳ glyph tracks the turn, and the answer re-renders by itself when it ends.

4Show tool calls

C-c C-t daniel-claudy-toggle-tool-lines

Shows or hides one [tool: ...] line per tool call Claude made.

Was broken by the transcript cache, in daniel-claude too. Fixed today.

5Jump to your last question

C-c C-j daniel-claudy-jump-to-question

Moves point to your last prompt and puts it at the top of the window.

6Send only the current line

C-c C-l daniel-claudy-tmux-send-current-line

Sends just the line at point, so notes elsewhere in the buffer stay unsent.

7Pick a session

daniel-claudy-view

Lists live sessions (C-u: every recent one), waiting first: status, project, name, last prompt, time. Picking one opens its transcript.

8No match? That's a new session

daniel-claudy-view, then RET on no match

Text that matches nothing becomes the name of a new session. Then you pick the directory from the projects Emacs knows.

9Queue the first prompt

C-c C-c while claude is still starting

A prompt sent before claude is up is queued and goes out once the session exists.

10Send a selection from any buffer

daniel-claudy-tmux-send-selection

Select text in any buffer and pick which Claude window gets it (or + new session).

Two open issues: windows with the same name and dir show as one row, and this view only updated after a manual C-c C-a.

11One-off question

daniel-claudy-direct-prompt

Runs claude -p (haiku by default) in the background with the selection and pops the answer in its own buffer. No session, no tmux.

12Usage limits

C-c C-u daniel-claudy-usage

Runs claude -p /usage in the background and shows your limits and account in every claudy mode line.

13Jump to the tmux pane

C-c C-o daniel-claudy-tmux-focus-pane

Switches the attached tmux client to this session's pane.

14End a session

C-c C-k daniel-claudy-exit-this-session

Asks first, then sends /exit (answers the worktree dialog too) and kills the buffer.

15Resume in this pane

C-c C-r daniel-claudy-resume

Sends /resume to this pane with a session you pick from the same repo, and shows that transcript.

The /exit command echo shows up as raw <command-name> text.

16Resume in a new window

daniel-claudy-resume-new-window

From any buffer: pick a recent session of this repo, get a new tmux window running claude --resume, plus its transcript.

17Refresh when Claude's turn ends

daniel-claudy-notify-finished (Stop hook)

The README's Stop hook calls this through emacsclient with the transcript path. Only the buffer you sent from refreshes. Shown with the file watcher off, so only the hook can refresh.
